To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the activation of the sympathetic system in the hypertension induced by chronic nitric acid synthase inhibition is mediated via angiotensin AT1 receptors in the nucleus tract solitarii.
angiotensin in NTS contributes to neurogenic component of hypertension caused by chronic NOS inhibition via AT1 receptor.
activation of the sympathetic nerve activity and renin- angiotensin system within the nucleus tracti solitarii contribute to the hypertension in rats with chronic nitric oxide synthease inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of angiotensin in neurogenic hypertension.
the role of angiotensin in neurogenic hypertension caused chronic nitric oxide (NO) synthase inhibition.
the role of the central nervous system (CNS) in the development of hypertension and in the maintenance of blood pressure in normal and hypertensive rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic nitric oxide deficiency leads to activation of the sympathetic and renin- angiotensin system, which contributes to the hypertension.

the angiotensin in NTS plays a role in the hypertension caused by nitric oxide synthetase inhibition via AT(1)-receptor activation and that this activation contributes, at least in part, to the sympathetic overactivity.

chronic nitric oxide synthesis inhibition causes activation of the sympathetic system and renin angiotensin system and that the activation of the rennin angiotensin is at least in part due to the angiotensin AT(1) receptor in the nucleus tract solitarii.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the angiotensin in nucleus tractus solitaris is involved in the neurogenic component of hypertension caused by chronic inhibition of NO synthase.

the renin- angiotensin system is activated in the nucleus tracti solitarii in response to chronic inhibition of nitric oxide synthesis and that this activation is at least partly responsible for the hypertension caused by nitric oxide synthesis inhibition.
chronic inhibition of NO synthesis in rats leads to a significant increase in blood pressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain renin-angio-tensin system is activated by nitric oxide deficiency and plays an important role in the pathogenesis of nitric oxide synthetase inhibition-induced hypertension.
the renin- angiotensin system within the NTS is activated in neurogenic hypertension caused via chronic nitric oxide inhibition.
angiotensin in NTS plays a role in the development of hypertension caused by chronic NOS inhibition.
